text: A philosopher who is a coherentist about justification but accepts a correspondence account of truth (as BonJour and Lehrer are usually read) is thereby committed to which of the following?
choices: Coherence among beliefs is what makes a belief true, while correspondence to the world is what justifies it.
Coherence among a subject's beliefs is what confers justification, while what makes a belief true is how the mind-independent world is.
Both the truth and the justification of a belief consist in its coherence with the subject's total system of beliefs.
Neither the truth nor the justification of a belief has any constitutive connection to coherence.
explanation: The coherence theory of truth (truth just is coherence within a system) must be kept distinct from coherentism about justification (coherence is the source of epistemic support). One can consistently hold the latter while rejecting the former, taking truth to be correspondence — indeed most contemporary coherentists about justification do exactly this. Option 0 inverts the two roles; option 2 conjoins the coherence theory of truth with coherentism; option 3 rejects both.
